saints.name: St. Albert the Great
saints.title: Bishop and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The Dominican polymath and teacher of Thomas Aquinas, called the Universal Doctor…
biography: Born about 1200 at Lauingen in Swabia, Albert entered the Order of Preachers and became one of the most learned men of the Middle Ages, mastering theology, philosophy, and the natural sciences with such range that he was called Doctor Universalis. At Paris and Cologne he taught the young Thomas Aquinas, whose genius he was the first to recognize and defend.

He served for a time as Bishop of Regensburg before returning to his studies and teaching, and he laboured to reconcile the newly recovered philosophy of Aristotle with Christian faith. He died at Cologne on 15 November 1280. He is a patron of natural scientists and students.
saints.knownFor: Uniting the natural sciences with theology and teaching St. Thomas Aquinas.

canonization.canonized: 1931 by Pope Pius XI, who declared him a Doctor of the Church
